findings.title: Non-immediate email cancellation waits for cron and can miss the send window
findings.body: When called without `immediateDelete`, this function only sets `cancelled: true` in the database and returns; it never calls SendGrid to cancel the scheduled send. Callers like `handleCancelBooking` and `requestReschedule` use this path for all email reminders. Because `scheduleEmailReminders` runs only every 15 minutes, a reminder whose `scheduledDate` is before the next cron run will already have been sent by SendGrid before the cron attempts cancellation. Cancelling a booking close to a reminder time can therefore still deliver the reminder. For reminders within the near-term window, SendGrid should be cancelled immediately or the cancellation must be event-driven.

findings.title: Workflow reminder cancellations are not awaited
findings.body: `updatedBookings.forEach` starts `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` but does not `await` them or collect their promises. This API handler returns right after `sendCancelledEmails`, so the process can end before the async Prisma update/delete or provider cancellation completes. An email reminder may never be set to `cancelled: true`, so the cron in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` never cancels it and the reminder can still be sent after cancellation. Use `await Promise.all(...)` over all reminder cancellations before returning.

findings.title: Request-reschedule reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget
findings.body: The `requestReschedule` mutation calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` inside `forEach` without awaiting their promises. In a serverless/TRPC context the mutation can resolve before the DB rows are marked or deleted and before Twilio/SendGrid operations finish, so reminders for the cancelled original booking can survive and still send. Collect and await these promises before the mutation returns.

findings.title: Disabling event types does not await reminder cancellation
findings.body: `remindersToDelete.flat().forEach(...)` invokes cancellation functions without awaiting their promises. Disabling an event type from a workflow can return to the client before the email reminder row is updated to `cancelled: true` or the SMS reminder is deleted. If the runtime shuts down after the response, the cancellation is lost and reminders for disabled workflows can still send. The same fire-and-forget pattern appears below when deleting/editing steps; all cancellation promises should be awaited before returning.

findings.title: Old reminders are cancelled before rescheduling succeeds
findings.body: This block sends cancellation for `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` before `eventManager.reschedule` runs. If the reschedule fails, for example due to a calendar or video integration error, the original booking remains active but its workflow reminders have already been cancelled. A live booking would then stop receiving reminders. Move this cancellation to after a successful reschedule, or compensate on failure if it must occur before.

findings.title: One SendGrid cancellation failure aborts all remaining cancellations in the cron run
findings.body: The entire `for` loop is inside one `try`/`catch`. If `client.request` throws for one reminder, execution jumps to the catch, skipping every remaining `remindersToCancel` entry and never awaiting the already-created Prisma delete promises. A single persistently bad `referenceId` or transient SendGrid error can block all other due cancellations in that run. Handle each reminder's SendGrid cancellation and delete independently (or continue on error) so one failure cannot prevent the rest.

findings.title: Immediate email cancellation leaves stale scheduled reminders in the database
findings.body: With `immediateDelete` true and a `referenceId`, this function sends the SendGrid cancel and returns without deleting or marking the `WorkflowReminder`. The reschedule path in `handleNewBooking` calls it this way and does not delete the row afterwards, leaving the old reminder as `scheduled: true` with `cancelled` null. Such rows accumulate and can be mistaken for active reminders later by workflow step edit/delete queries. Delete the row or set `cancelled: true` after successful SendGrid cancellation when the caller will not cascade a delete.
